_comment: THE ESTATE DECLARATION — copy this, fill it in, keep it OUT of this repository.
Point setup/* at it with MODX_ESTATE=/path/to/your-estate.json.
With no MODX_ESTATE set, the software installs a generic empty estate (setup/estate.py _DEFAULT).
Every value below is fictional and exists to show the shape.

web_context.name: Web
web_context.description: MODX's own context — always exists; setup/01 only relabels it

_contexts: protected: true means setup/04 access-controls this context's pages and files. A protected context MUST also name `home` — the ALIAS of the page a signed-in member lands on (setup/03 creates one called `home` in every context). Without it the context refuses anonymous callers correctly and then has nowhere to send a member, which nothing reports. A public context needs no home.
_users: (username, fullname, email, sso_only). EMAIL is what Google SSO matches on, so for an SSO user it must equal their Google account exactly. Group membership is NOT set here — setup/04 owns it, from groups below.
_groups: group name -> [contexts it may enter, users it starts with]
_domains: context -> public host. 'contexts' may list MORE than 'contexts' above: a context added later by setup/11-add-context still needs a hostname. 'bench_zone' is the bench zone; each context gets <context>.<bench_zone>. Omit bench_zone if you have no bench. 'bench_ports' gives each context a port for a `php -S` bench (setup/bench-server.php, profile 'local'); omit it if you serve the bench through a web server. 'bench_scheme' is http or https and defaults to http — set it to https when the bench sits behind a TLS edge, or MODx generates absolute links on the wrong scheme while the edge quietly redirects them back.
